content:
Apple's biggest product launch event of the year is just around the corner, and more than 10 new products are set to debut in the near future. Here are the five new products I'm most looking forward to.

iPhone Ultra

The first foldable iPhone is about to arrive, combining the iPhone and iPad mini into one device—truly exciting.

Although the hardware specs have been heavily leaked, the software on the iPhone Ultra is the key to the overall experience. I'm very eager to see how Apple tunes iOS 27 to be both natively smooth and capable of delivering greater functionality in a foldable form factor.

I've never used a foldable smartphone before, but based on everything I've read, this product form factor seems to be the direction of the future. Apple has clearly thought things through carefully before entering the foldable market, and I have high hopes that it can live up to the wait.

HomePad

For years I've been hoping Apple would take the smart home market seriously. In late 2024, Mark Gurman was the first to exclusively break the detailed report on the 'HomePad', signalling that this shift is about to happen.

The HomePad appeals to me on many fronts. I'm looking forward to features like Apple Photos slideshow playback, security camera functions, Siri AI, and Apple Music playback with lyrics display, among many others.

The delay of Siri AI has made the wait for the HomePad much longer than expected. However, all signs indicate that the launch is imminent, and I'm ready to witness how Apple maps out a new era of smart home development through the HomePad and other new Home products.

The all-new Apple TV 4K

It's been four years since the previous-generation Apple TV 4K was released. Although the device doesn't need to be updated every year, the rise of AI technology holds tremendous potential for a comprehensive experience overhaul.

I'm eager to see how Siri AI, a more powerful chip, and other hardware and software upgrades come together to deliver an Apple TV experience worth upgrading for.

With the all-new Apple TV 4K launching alongside the HomePad with a camera, I'm also curious to see whether earlier rumours about a camera-equipped version will come true. Being able to make FaceTime calls on the big screen without needing an iPhone in the future would be a fantastic user experience.

MacBook Ultra

I've been using an iPad Pro as my primary computer for over a decade. One of the major reasons I made this switch in 2015 was that the Mac always lagged behind the iPad in terms of innovative hardware and software features.

After Apple brought its own chips to the Mac, some of these issues have been addressed. macOS is also increasingly updating in sync with iOS and iPadOS. However, the Mac still has plenty of elements that feel stuck in the past rather than looking toward the future.

I expect the MacBook Ultra to change that. Adding touch functionality, plus an OLED display, Dynamic Island, a brand-new design, and possibly even cellular connectivity options—all of this is very appealing. This is the Mac update I've been waiting for, and I can't wait to see what surprises Apple has in store.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4

For this year's new Apple Watch, I still haven't decided between the Series 12 and the Ultra 4. But regardless of which one I choose, I'm very much looking forward to the new models, because of one key rumoured upgrade: an all-new S-series chip designed for the AI era.

Apple Watch chips don't get updated often. Although Apple makes small improvements to the S-series chip every year, significant CPU performance gains only happen roughly every three years. So the last time the Watch chip saw a notable performance leap was with the S9 back in 2023.

However, rumours suggest that this year's Watch models will feature a more powerful all-new chip. This will be the first chip designed specifically for the AI era, and launching it alongside Siri AI makes for perfect timing.

Which upcoming Apple product are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments section.
